scenario_title: Engine upgrade applied immediately at peak
title: Connection failures on cloud-api
impact: Requests failed while connections were refused on cloud-api
symptom: [ANOMALY] cloud-api 2026-03-25 19:23-22:33: cloud-api: 328 of 397 log lines were non-INFO between 2026-03-25 19:23 and 2026-03-25 22:33 UTC (peak error ratio 1.0 vs baseline median 0.0). 2 error templates, 1 first seen in this span. Peak p95 latency 1.975 s vs baseline band up to 0.453 s.
error_templates: Unexpected exception while calling meta-db: FATAL: sorry, too many clients already

_templates.macro: Terraform change upgraded {svc} with apply_immediately = true; the Multi-AZ failover happened at peak and JVM clients kept stale connections and DNS for minutes.
_templates.remediation: Set apply_immediately back to false (maintenance window); cap JVM DNS TTL at 30 s; enable pool validation.

culprit.diff:
@@ -43,3 +43,3 @@ aws_db_instance.meta_db
 resource "aws_db_instance" "meta_db" {
-  apply_immediately = "false"
+  apply_immediately = "true"
   tags = local.tags

rca.macro: Terraform change upgraded meta-db with apply_immediately = true; the Multi-AZ failover happened at peak and JVM clients kept stale connections and DNS for minutes.
rca.micro: infra/meta-db.tf:44 sets rds_apply_immediately false -> true on aws_db_instance.meta_db.
rca.remediation: Set apply_immediately back to false (maintenance window); cap JVM DNS TTL at 30 s; enable pool validation.

action_items: Require a reviewed `terraform plan` and a CloudWatch alarm for the changed AWS resource.
Alert on the error signature `<*> <*> <*> HTTP/1.1" status: <*> len: <*> time: <*>`.
